substanceAudit.why: Three input corpora were rejected earlier today for holding records that were called initial states but named no state — per-state keys carrying only a slug, the class name, NOT-AUTHORED, and the class name again. The crude form of that defect is plainly absent here, so I tested the refined form: whether each stateNamed merely restates its member name at greater length.
substanceAudit.result: It does not. Each state adds fixture-shaping content the member name does not carry. EV-1's member is the property 'preview result is not a sealed Run'; the state names the artifact that will hold it — terminal-result bytes showing the absence of the label. EV-2's 'no silent promotion' becomes a record about later surfaces. EV-3's 'not G19 durable state-byte class' becomes the two concrete durable classes the result must not be written as. In each case the state tells a future fixture author something the member name does not.
substanceAudit.trimmingIsConservativeNotLossy: Each state starts after its exactByteIntent's 'Once authored:' preamble, dropping 'digest-pinned' from EV-1, 'the same pinned results, paired with a record that' from EV-2, and 'a not-that-gate record that' from EV-3. Every dropped fragment describes the future fixture's custody or evidence form rather than the initial state, and this corpus authors no fixture bytes, so carrying 'digest-pinned' would have been the over-claim. None of the three fields is marked as verbatim, so none carries a byte-equality claim it fails.

boundaryAudit.sealedRunClass: This is the constraint EV-1 states against itself — 'This specification does not invent a sealed-Run class against which to compare; it retains the absence of that label.' The corpus honours it two ways. Structurally, no class is defined anywhere: no schema, no fields, no membership rule, no discriminator, nothing a fixture could compare against. Textually, all nine 'sealed' occurrences are refusals, quotations of the live cell, or the absence-of-label construction EV-1 requires; the phrase 'sealed-Run class' appears five times and every one is a refusal.
boundaryAudit.g19: Seven G19 occurrences: four refusals or not-authored entries, one quotation of the live evidence cell inside the D-153 role, and two in state three. State three uses G19's own vocabulary, and I checked it is quoted rather than invented — 'rebuildable cache/index' and 'operational metadata' both appear in G19 v1, which reproduces against the pin G27 v1 carries. The corpus defines no G19 class, adds no G19 member, and scores nothing, which is what EV-3's passProperty reserves when it says the member does not score G19 cross-class negatives.
boundaryAudit.fxAuthoringStaysOpen: The corpus states in its authorityClaim that it does not close leftover-design of G27 fixture implementations, and the pinned gate join holds OBL-G27-FX-AUTHORING at leftoverDesign true as the only open obligation on DR-G27. Read at source, not taken from the subject.

This one does not: it names initial states within the already-named class, which is the OBL-G27-FX-AUTHORING remainder the join leaves open.
boundaryAudit.d153: Verified in the adopted COORD entry. D-153 assigns DR-G27 PREVIEW-ANALYZE-NOT-SEALED-RUN, it owns DR-131 NT-6 only, and NT-6 leftover-design closes with the remainder at G27 execution. independence.theRiskThisCycle: This is the sixth input corpus in seven cycles, and the three rejections all turned on one defect — states that named no state. The risk is that the test has collapsed into a presence check, so that anything with populated stateNamed fields passes. I answered it by making the containment test the work rather than the inspection: each state was matched byte-for-byte against its cited source, the member count was checked against the live register rather than against the harness alone, and the refined form of the defect was tested separately from the crude one.
independence.residualRisk: I set the standard this family is measured against, in the G16 verdict, and I have now applied it six times. The decomposition judgment in particular — one state here, two at G24's EV-3, eight at G07's EV-1 — rests on my reading of what each source clause signals, and a reviewer who had not set that standard would be better placed to say whether the three readings cohere. I have stated the rule and the three applications so the coherence can be checked rather than taken.

coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Twenty-two attacks run, none landed. Custody holds: subject d4dd7e61 at 0444, 4911 bytes, unmoved at both ends; HEAD never left 5d5d778 and the artifact's head equals it; live required-now 26 of 26 at file 08 condition 4, which names G27 under D-153; file 08 and COORD unmodified. All five cited pins reproduce and the artifact's five 64-hex strings are exactly those pins. Three named initial states against G27 v1's three retained-evidence members, one-to-one in both directions, and each stateNamed is a byte-exact substring of the exactByteIntent of the member its own source field names — verified by containment, not by reading. Two checks decide whether three is the right number rather than merely a self-consistent one, and both were made against the live register rather than the harness alone: G27 v1's liveCellVerbatim splits on semicolons into exactly three members and file 08 line 363's evidence cell is byte-identical to it, and the single class phrase, 'no-silent-promotion corpus (DR-131 NT-6)', is a byte-exact substring of the file 08 harness cell. G27 v1 carries no namedCorpusNotAuthored field, unlike its G24 sibling, so that phrase had to be split out of the live cell, and the split takes the corpus segment whole. I tested the refined form of the defect that sank three sibling corpora today — whether each state merely restates its member name at greater length — and it fails: every state adds content a future fixture author needs and the member name does not carry. The two boundaries the dispatch protects hold structurally, not just verbally. No sealed-Run class exists anywhere in the file: no schema, no fields, no membership rule, no discriminator, and all five occurrences of the phrase are refusals, while the states use the absence-of-label construction EV-1 explicitly mandates when it says the specification retains the absence of that label rather than inventing a class to compare against. G19 is named seven times without a single G19 class defined, member added or thing scored; state three's vocabulary is quoted through EV-3 and I confirmed both terms appear in G19 v1, which reproduces against the pin G27 v1 carries for it. OBL-G27-FX-AUTHORING stays open at the pinned join, read at source, and the catalog does not reach for OBL-G27-NAMED-CORPUS, which that same join already records as specified-not-leftover. D-153 verified in the adopted text: DR-G27 owns DR-131 NT-6 only and NT-6 leftover-design closes with the remainder at G27 execution, which the subject declines to reopen and does not claim to have closed; NT-6 is the only NT the file names. One judgment is worth recording for cross-verdict coherence. EV-3 joins two G19 durable classes with 'or' and the corpus keeps them in one state, where at G24 I accepted a two-way split of that corpus's EV-3 and at G07 an eight-way split of its EV-1. The rule in all three is the same — follow the source's own signal — and here the signal is 'a not-that-gate record', singular, with the result required to be in neither class rather than one of them. Disclosure: both Claude-lane verdicts this corpus pins are my lane's, I checked each claimed verdict against the review bytes rather than accepting the claim, and I set the standard this family is measured against in the G16 verdict, now applied six times across three rejections and three acceptances.
